name: svg-path
title: Heart icon from an SVG path
summary: A filled red heart drawn from one SVG path string of six cubic curves.
prompt: Draw a red heart icon from an SVG path string.
teaches: Draw a vector icon by passing SVG path data (M, C, Z) straight to drawPath
A path is filled with the current paint; the default paint style is fill
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre
pitfalls: Only drawPath takes an SVG string: the same string in resources.paths or a `path` command becomes an EMPTY path in the Java reference (and json2rc matches it), so nothing draws; use the op-list form there

The Java reference parser writes an SVG string path with a 1024-float zero-padded buffer (about 4 KB per path) and 0,0 as each segment's start point, so its bytes differ from json2rc's although both render the same; prefer primitives or pathCreate for small shapes
Path coordinates are canvas dp, not a 24x24 viewBox: scale the icon's numbers (or wrap it in a scale) to the canvas

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())

snippets.note: drawPath with an SVG d string: a heart from six cubic Bezier segments

check.describe: A symmetric red heart centred on a dark background. Resized, it scales to the shorter side and stays centred.

java_difference: SVG path strings: the Java writer pads each to 1024 floats (RemotePathBase.getPath returns the backing array)
